extracted.intended_audience: editors, journalists, writers, and readers interested in inclusive/conscious language and style
extracted.subtask_description: An index/listing of short articles and essays about conscious/inclusive language and style for journalists, editors, authors, and content creators. The page collects topic-focused pieces that each address a specific wording, stylistic, or editorial concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture book imagery and unconscious bias
rubrics_metrics.description: For children’s books, a copyeditor looks at more than words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider images (not just text) when assessing unconscious bias in children’s literature; visual elements matter for representation and stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity reads for Jewish characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Building trust with readers by providing a clear why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authors request or respond to sensitivity reads about Jewish representation, explain the rationale behind suggested changes to build trust with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overemphasizing gender in obituaries
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s time to show respect by not overemphasizing gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rethink courtesy titles and gendered emphasis in obituaries to show respect without overemphasizing gender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering poverty: what to avoid and how to get it right
rubrics_metrics.description: A tip sheet from Journalist’s Resource to help journalists think more deeply about how they select and cover stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should follow practical tips to avoid harmful tropes and to cover poverty with depth, context, and dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing terminology for pregnancy/fetal coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Are “Fetus” and “Unborn Child” Interchangeable? Guidance from Rewire.News and the 2018 Associated Press Stylebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be deliberate with terms like 'fetus' vs 'unborn child'; follow established style guidance (e.g., AP) and consider context and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid default assumptions in pop-culture criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: On the practice of assuming that straightness and Whiteness are culturally neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should avoid language that treats straightness and Whiteness as the default or neutral cultural norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine culinary vocabulary for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: On the importance of using conscious language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review food-related terminology for cultural insensitivity or exclusion and choose language that is respectful and precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hyphenate 'Asian American'
rubrics_metrics.description: Drop the Hyphen in 'Asian American' — On the historical divisiveness of an unnecessary punctuation mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using a hyphen in 'Asian American' because the hyphen has historically been divisive; treat it as two-word compound without hyphenation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ageist language about young people
rubrics_metrics.description: Young People and Ageist Language — Changing our attitudes toward children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and writers should avoid ageist descriptors that demean or infantilize young people and reassess assumptions about youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid imprecise education descriptors
rubrics_metrics.description: The False Divide Between 'Well Educated' and 'Less Educated' — When imprecise language confuses, conflates, and excludes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from broad labels like 'well educated' vs 'less educated' that obscure nuance and can exclude or conflate groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive style for covering sexual violence
rubrics_metrics.description: From Bias and Blame to Balance: Sensitive Style for Covering Sexual Violence — Basic guidelines for fair and accurate reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow sensitive-style guidelines that avoid blame, provide context, protect survivors' dignity, and aim for balanced, accurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid carnivorous/metaphorical language that excludes
rubrics_metrics.description: Putting Language on a Meat-Free Diet — Carnivorous expressions serve to exclude, not include.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of meat-based metaphors and idioms that may exclude or alienate people; choose inclusive figurative language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalize racial identifiers appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalizing for Equality — When Black and White are used as racial terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use capitalization (e.g., 'Black') when words are used as racial identifiers to acknowledge identity and respect conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make web images accessible to blind users
rubrics_metrics.description: Making Web Images Accessible to People Who Are Blind — Small touches that help screen-reader users feel included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add alt text and other accessibility features to web images so screen-reader users are included; implement small, practical accessibility measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer direct inclusive language over euphemism
rubrics_metrics.description: Euphemism Is Dead — Why inclusive language in the age of Trump means speaking the ugly truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid euphemisms that obscure harm; use direct language when necessary to be inclusive and truthful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak up against casual hate
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Speak Up Against Casual Hate — Guidance from the Southern Poverty Law Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recommended strategies (e.g., those from SPLC) to intervene or respond to casual hateful speech in constructive ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware that bias-free language can exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: When Bias-Free Language Excludes — And when biased language promotes visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that attempts at bias-free language can sometimes erase or exclude groups; balance neutrality with visibility where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sexist language that harms multiple genders
rubrics_metrics.description: How Sexist Language Hurts Men — Stereotyping one gender means simultaneously stereotyping another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that sexist language can harm all genders; avoid stereotypes and phrasing that reinforce gendered assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assumptions in 'coming out' language
rubrics_metrics.description: When 'Coming Out' Puts People in the Closet — The problem with using language shrouded in assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with 'coming out' narratives and language that assume uniform experiences; acknowledge diversity of experiences and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and consult disability style guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Disability Style Guide Expands Coverage — Basic guidelines for covering the disability community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow disability-specific style guidance to cover disability communities respectfully and accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult AP and Chicago guides on sexist language
rubrics_metrics.description: AP and Chicago on Sexist Language — We might not get it right, but we must try. Notes and resources (and tweets!) from Karen Yin’s presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to mainstream style manuals (AP, Chicago) and expert resources to reduce sexist language; expect ongoing revisions and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trans terminology for sensitivity and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Trans Terminology 201 — Talking about members of the transgender community with sensitivity and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use current, respectful trans terminology; prioritize sensitivity and factual accuracy when writing about transgender people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit hedging to preserve confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Pruning Hedges: Editing for Confidence — When hedging gets in the way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce unnecessary hedging in copy that undermines clarity or confidence while preserving nuance where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid language that erases bisexual people
rubrics_metrics.description: When Bisexual People Marry — How biased language promotes stereotypes and erasure of bisexual people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with wording around marriage and relationships that can perpetuate stereotypes or erase bisexual identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate terminology with humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibrating Terminology — Accepting the challenges inherent in understanding one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept the difficulty of perfect terminology; calibrate word choice thoughtfully and be open to revision and dialogue.
